preheader: Midterm data center backlash, Agility hits Nasdaq, and Anthropic files Q3 numbers.

lead.headline: Voter pushback stalls data center projects after midterm elections
lead.body: Voters rejected 40 out of 41 local ballot measures related to data center construction across the country in Tuesday's elections. In response to the political pushback, OpenAI announced new policies promising greater transparency, community involvement, and local jobs to salvage its infrastructure expansion plans.
lead.why: Infrastructure access will decide which AI companies survive. If you want to invest in or build AI startups, keep an eye on power constraints and local municipal zoning battles.

stories.headline: Amazon replaces Grubhub with Uber Eats for Prime members
stories.body: Amazon named Uber Eats its official restaurant delivery partner for Prime subscribers in the United States. The agreement brings an end to Amazon's previous partnership with Grubhub.
stories.why: Platform distribution deals can reshape consumer behavior quickly. Watch how platform bundling affects customer acquisition costs in your marketing and strategy coursework.

stories.headline: Market volatility gauge spikes 55 percent in sudden surge
stories.body: The CBOE Volatility Index jumped 55 percent, marking its largest single-day surge since January 2021. Readings above 16 typically indicate that the S&P 500 could swing by more than 1 percent in either direction.
stories.why: A spiking VIX points to choppy markets ahead. When managing your own portfolio, wide swings mean you should be cautious with market orders and short-term positions.

stories.headline: Agility lists on Nasdaq as the first public humanoid robotics pure-play
stories.body: Agility began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after completing a reverse merger. The listing makes it the first publicly traded pure-play humanoid robotics company, defying predictions a year ago from rival Figure AI that it would run out of cash.
stories.why: Public market listings establish valuation benchmarks for entire tech niches. Future robotics and hardware pitch decks will now be judged against Agility's public financials.

stories.headline: Anthropic posts $16.96 billion in Q3 revenue in amended IPO filing
stories.body: Anthropic filed an updated registration statement with the SEC showing third-quarter revenue of $16.96 billion and a smaller net loss than the prior period. The company cautioned prospective investors in its prospectus that it cannot guarantee rapid revenue growth will continue.
stories.why: IPO filings give you a rare look into private AI economics, gross margins, and compute spending before shares trade publicly.

stories.headline: Cutting entry-level roles for AI creates long-term talent risks
stories.body: Many corporate managers now look to AI tools to take over drafting, research, and data summaries traditionally given to interns and new hires. However, removing those entry-level roles risks breaking the apprenticeship model required to develop future senior leaders.
stories.why: For consulting and corporate recruiting, focus on soft skills, client handling, and strategic synthesis that software cannot replace.

stories.headline: McKinsey survey finds 87 percent of organizations hit by threat incidents
stories.body: A study by McKinsey & Company found that 87 percent of surveyed organizations experienced at least one threat incident over the past 24 months. The firm noted that many companies still carry serious preparedness gaps for risks outside conventional IT cybersecurity.
stories.why: Operational risk management and corporate resilience are expanding fast inside consulting firms, creating hiring demand for analyst positions.

stories.headline: 17-year-old Maaya Revathi reaches WTA quarterfinals in Chennai
stories.body: Indian wildcard Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi beat world No. 277 Weronika Falkowska 6-4, 6-3 at the WTA 250 Chennai Open. She became the first Indian woman to reach a tour-level singles quarterfinal since Sania Mirza did so in 2012.

stories.headline: Lorenzo Musetti defeats newly crowned world No. 1 Alexander Zverev
stories.body: Alexander Zverev lost his opening match as the world's top-ranked player, falling 7-6(5), 6-2 to Lorenzo Musetti just days after climbing to the No. 1 spot on Monday.

term.name: Reverse merger
term.definition: A transaction where a private company goes public by merging into an existing public entity, usually a dormant shell company. It allows the private firm to trade on an exchange without going through the lengthy, expensive roadshow of a standard initial public offering. Agility Robotics used this structure today to list its humanoid robotics business on the Nasdaq.

serve.headline: Kabilio raised €10M to automate accounting firm workflows
serve.body: Barcelona startup Kabilio builds AI agents designed to handle repetitive bookkeeping tasks and chase receipts for accounting firms. The seed round was led by Picus Capital and Visionaries, with support from Spanish public innovation agency CDTI.
questions: What daily administrative task in your business classes could a focused AI agent eliminate?
Why would accounting firms prefer vertical agents over general tools like ChatGPT?
If automated agents handle receipt collection, what higher-value advisory services should junior accountants pitch instead?
